title: ANA 201 : BACK OF THE BODY INTRO
subject: ANA 201

questions.question: What is the name given to the muscles that attach the shoulder girdle to the axial skeleton posteriorly?
questions.explanation: The text states these muscles are called posterior axio-appendicular muscles.

questions.question: Removal of the scapula in malignant disease like fibrosarcoma requires detailed knowledge of what?
options: Only the bones of the back
Muscles, nerves, and vessels on the back
Only the skin and superficial fascia
questions.explanation: The text notes this removal requires detailed knowledge of the muscles, nerves, and vessels on the back.

questions.question: Which structure is considered the most important surface landmark on the back?
questions.explanation: The text explicitly states that the scapula is the most important surface landmark on the back.

questions.question: Vertically, the scapula extends from which rib to which rib?
questions.explanation: The text notes that the scapula vertically extends from the 2nd to the 7th rib.

questions.question: The superior angle of the scapula lies at the level of which vertebral spine?
questions.explanation: The text states the superior angle of the scapula lies opposite the spine of the T2 vertebra.

questions.question: The root of the spine of the scapula lies at the level of which vertebra?
questions.explanation: The root of the spine lies at the level of the T3 vertebra.

questions.question: The inferior angle of the scapula lies at the level of which vertebra?
questions.explanation: The inferior angle of the scapula lies at the level of the T7 vertebra.

questions.question: Approximately how many muscles are attached to the processes and fossae of the scapula?
questions.explanation: The text notes the scapula is freely mobile as about 15 muscles are attached to its processes and fossae.

questions.question: Which rib is palpable immediately inferior to the inferior angle of the scapula?
questions.explanation: The eighth rib is palpable immediately inferior to the inferior angle of the scapula.

questions.question: The lower ribs can be counted from which rib?
questions.explanation: The text states the eighth rib is palpable immediately inferior to the inferior angle, and the lower ribs can be counted from it.

questions.question: How far above the iliac crest can the twelfth rib be palpated if it projects beyond the lateral margin of the erector spinae muscle?
questions.explanation: The text states the twelfth rib can be palpated about 3 cm above the iliac crest.

questions.question: The posterior superior iliac spine may be felt in a shallow dimple about how far from the median line?
questions.explanation: The text states it may be felt in a shallow dimple of skin above the buttock, about 5 cm from the median line.

questions.question: The back of the sacrum lies between which two structures?
questions.explanation: The back of the sacrum lies between the right and left dimples.

questions.question: Which bone is slightly movable and may be felt deep between the buttocks in the natal cleft?
questions.explanation: The coccyx is described as a slightly movable bone felt deep in the natal cleft.

questions.question: Which vertebra is known as the vertebra prominens and is readily felt at the root of the neck?
questions.explanation: The spine of the 7th cervical vertebra is called the vertebra prominens.

questions.question: What demarcates the junction between the head and neck posteriorly?
options: External occipital protuberance and superior nuchal lines
Mastoid process and inferior nuchal lines
Spine of C7 and ligamentum nuchae
questions.explanation: These bony features demarcate the junction between the head and neck posteriorly.

questions.question: The external occipital protuberance is felt in the midline on which part of the body?
questions.explanation: The text describes it as a bony projection felt in the midline on the back of the head.

questions.question: The nuchal groove furrow extends from the external occipital protuberance to the spine of which vertebra?
questions.explanation: The nuchal groove furrow extends from the external occipital protuberance to the spine of C7 vertebra.

questions.question: What is the median fibrous partition on the back of the neck called?
questions.explanation: The text defines the ligamentum nuchae as the median fibrous partition on the back of the neck.

questions.question: The ligamentum nuchae separates the short cervical spines from what?
questions.explanation: The text states it separates the short cervical spines from the skin.

questions.question: The cutaneous nerves on the back are derived from which rami of the spinal nerves?
questions.explanation: The cutaneous nerves on the back are derived from the posterior rami of the spinal nerves.

questions.question: Up to which vertebral level is cutaneous innervation of the back provided by medial branches of the posterior rami?
questions.explanation: Up to T6, the cutaneous innervation is provided by medial branches.

questions.question: Below T6, the cutaneous innervation of the back is provided by which branches?
questions.explanation: Below T6, the cutaneous innervation is provided by lateral branches.

questions.question: The lateral branches below T6 emerge in line with the lateral edge of which muscle?
questions.explanation: These lateral branches emerge in line with the lateral edge of the erector spinae muscle.

questions.question: The cutaneous branches of the upper three lumbar nerves supply the skin of which region?
questions.explanation: These branches turn down over the iliac crest to supply the skin of the gluteal region.

questions.question: The posterior rami of which of the following spinal nerves do NOT give any cutaneous branches?
questions.explanation: The posterior rami of C1, C7, C8, L4, and L5 do not give any cutaneous branches.

questions.question: The posterior rami of which lumbar spinal nerves do NOT give any cutaneous branches?
questions.explanation: The text lists L4 and L5 among those that do not give any cutaneous branches.

questions.question: The approximate level of the highest point of the iliac crest is at which vertebral spine?
questions.explanation: The table indicates the highest point of the iliac crest is at the L4 level.

questions.question: The posterior-superior iliac spine corresponds to which vertebral level?
questions.explanation: The table indicates the posterior-superior iliac spine is at the S2 level.

questions.question: The crest of the spine of the scapula meets its medial border at the level of which vertebra?
questions.explanation: The table indicates this meeting point is at the T3 level.
